A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MonoTAKD. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original KITTI and nuScenes detection results, component ablations, convergence curves and additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original detection results and reports additional architecture, backbone, detector and computational-efficiency experiments.

M1.justification: The teacher/teaching-assistant/student framework, IMD, CMRD and SAM remain. However, FFM is described as three 3×3 convolutional layers in v1 Section 3.5 and two convolutional layers in v2 Section 3.4, a limited reported architecture revision. MonoTAKD-Lite corresponds to the existing IMD-only configuration rather than an entirely new distillation method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate KITTI Car, Pedestrian and Cyclist detection, semi-supervised training with KITTI raw, and multi-view detection on nuScenes. V2's additional architectures and backbone experiments remain within this coverage; its raw-data subset revision concerns the protocol.

E2.justification: Comparator membership changes substantially. V2 Table 1 adds methods including MonoNeRD, MonoUNI, OccupancyM3D and MonoCD while removing several earlier KITTI baselines. Its nuScenes Table 2 adds BEVDistill, DistillBEV, STXD and LabelDistill comparisons. The Pedestrian/Cyclist comparison also removes CMKD from v1 Table 2 while adding newer methods in v2 Table C1.

E3.justification: Reported KITTI raw training changes from 42K unlabeled examples in v1 Section 4.3 to the 22K Eigen clean subset in v2 Appendix A. V2 introduces explicit ResNet50/101 nuScenes configurations, broader teacher/assistant/student combinations, and speed/FLOPs evaluation. It drops the five nuScenes true-positive error metrics reported in v1. These are substantial protocol changes, although the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds assistant/student architecture comparisons, computational-efficiency analysis, backbone comparisons and detector-transfer analysis in Tables 3, 6, D3 and D4. Conversely, v1's assistant-training study, teacher-to-student performance-drop comparison and additional qualitative cases disappear (Tables A1/B2 and Figure C2). The convergence analysis is retained and moved from Figure B1 to Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Headline KITTI Car AP3D remains 27.91/19.43/16.51, and the proposed method's non-car and KITTI raw scores also remain unchanged. Nevertheless, v2 adds many architecture-specific and efficiency results, including BEVDepth-R101 with TAKD at 0.564 NDS/0.466 mAP. Reported SAM baseline AP3D changes from 30.36/19.80/16.53 to 31.36/20.80/16.53, while several BEV ablation scores and nuScenes error results disappear. Results under different configurations do not establish same-setting gains.

T1.justification: No theorem or proof is added, and most equations are streamlined restatements. However, v1 Equation 5 defines residuals as a masked absolute teacher–assistant difference, whereas v2's text following Equation 4 specifies subtraction and binarization without the explicit absolute value. It is unclear whether this revises the mathematical target or abbreviates the earlier definition.

C1.justification: The central distillation contribution and KITTI state-of-the-art claim remain. V2 promotes multi-view and unlabeled-data generalization into the abstract and contribution list, and adds an explicit claim of competitive performance without SAM. These broaden the emphasized contributions without replacing the paper's central claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations involving architecture heterogeneity, prediction-head compatibility, backbone complexity and specialization for monocular versus multi-view detection. Section 5 discusses limitations of comparisons across different settings and computational costs. Section 4.3 also newly argues that the proposed components do not extend training time, substantially expanding the earlier interpretation of distillation effectiveness.

D1.justification: V2 specifies ResNet50, adds a planned code-repository link and raw-subset details, and changes reported KITTI hardware from two Titan XP GPUs to one. More consequentially, it removes v1 Appendix A's 20/45-epoch feature-only warm-up schedules and additional teaching-assistant training instructions. Many other hyperparameters are simply relocated to Appendix B; the missing schedules represent a substantive loss of reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds an explicit distinction from Mirzadeh et al.'s teacher-assistant distillation and discusses adaptation modules and regularization more directly. References are refreshed with works such as STXD, LabelDistill, OccupancyM3D and MonoCD, while several older works disappear. The overarching positioning around the cross-modal representation gap remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten, with simplified notation and revised terminology. Related work is divided into additional subsections, implementation details move into the supplement, a Discussion section is added, and the appendix is reorganized. This is substantial editorial restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the single-column layout with a two-column format and extensively restructures tables and figure placement. It adds the residual-feature display in Figure 4 and new comparison tables, removes several old displays, moves the convergence plot into the main text, and relocates the retained detection and BEV visualizations to Figures E1/E2.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the evidence through broader distillation comparisons, architecture studies and explicit computational costs. However, it removes the warm-up schedules needed to interpret the retained convergence curves while adding a no-extra-training-time claim. It also changes the stated raw-data training subset without explaining the unchanged scores, and Appendix A calls 3,769 images the test set despite Section 4.1 distinguishing that validation count from 7,518 test images. These benefits and material reproducibility ambiguities prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
